title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 48
summary: Personally inspect 32 roots: 30 additions and two scope exclusions.
notes: Root personally ran 32 cross-platform searches yielding 374 hits and 371 repository roots. Inspected 32 selected roots and prepared 30 additions and two scope exclusions. No discovery worker used. Baseline is 3536789038b4a864784f5ff8ffd0413b1a41e3f3 with 4253 projects. No upstream code, binaries, emulators, installers or media were executed. Ingestion findings: same product names can denote independent engines (two OpenSWOS projects), unrelated modern products (SATURN chart editor), or hardware-only research (Mac analog board). Read explicit status before interpreting byte-exactness as universal decoder success: tbx documents a residual corpus mismatch. Old .ASC files and extensionless paths can contain real assembly; absent README is not absent implementation. Generic emulators/debuggers are not BAKED EMULATION game ports. Native API/hardware shims do not alone justify that tag. Source comments can contradict benefit claims (VideoDespeckle), and Java tools may launch Windows-native helpers. Distinguish planned ports/debugger features from implemented capabilities and preserve legacy-project successor attribution. Concurrent canonical BAKED EMULATION migration is separate engineering work; this discovery input creates no legacy execution tags. Pinning is a review snapshot, not a promise upstream heads remain current.
